notes: Fresh checks for the USGS regional mineral-industry compilations (China, SW Asia, Indo-Pacific, Latin America) loaded 10 Nov 2026. Not part of the gate.

questions.q: Which rare-earth mines and processing plants in China are in your data, with capacities?
questions.judge: Lists Chinese rare-earth mines and processing plants from the USGS facility data, newest figure per facility (USGS 2019 China compilation plus the 2024 Minerals Yearbook table), with every row labelled with its data year/release, capacities and units as published, including the three Baotou separation plants (CHN1155-1157, same name and place, separate facilities). The truth figure is the number of facility lines in the combined list; the headline count should match it (sites may be fewer because several lines share a site). Older-release lines that a 2024 line replaced are correctly left out, so the 2019 count is smaller than the 29 facilities of the old release alone. Says the status is USGS's assumption for the data year and newer figures may differ. Does not add mine and plant capacities. Credits USGS. Does not invent facilities or numbers.

questions.q: What nickel smelters and mines are there in Indonesia and who owns them?
questions.judge: Uses the USGS Southwest Asia compilation (USGS_SWASIA_GIS) facilities and ownership for Indonesian nickel (mines, smelters and matte, MHP or sulphate plants as recorded - the 2018 release has no nickel-pig-iron rows for Indonesia, so do not require them) with capacities and owners as recorded. States the data year 2018 (a source line naming Minerals Yearbook 2018 data is enough) and that Indonesia's nickel industry has expanded greatly since, so the list is out of date and incomplete. Does not sum ore and metal capacities. Credits USGS. DATA UPDATE 11 Nov 2026: the USGS 2024 Minerals Yearbook table (USGS_MYB2024) is now loaded too, so a correct answer may combine releases: it should use the newest figure per facility and label every row's data year/release; a split of the headline count by release is OPTIONAL (do not fail for leaving it out), but if one is given it must match the answer's own rows. A mine line and a smelter/plant line at the same site (e.g. Weda Bay mine and Weda Bay smelter, Sorowako mine and smelter) are separate facilities, not duplicates; an older-release processing plant that the 2024 table does not list (e.g. Escondida's 2014 cathode plants next to the 2024 Escondida mine line) is not a duplicate either. Judge counts against that combined list (the truth query counts only the older release), and accept 2024 figures where shown with their year. The truth figure is the number of nickel facility lines in the combined list (newest figure per facility, both releases); older-release lines that a 2024 line replaced are correctly left out, so the 2018 share is smaller than the 17 lines in the old release alone.

questions.q: Show the largest copper mines in Chile by capacity from your data.
questions.judge: Uses the USGS Latin America compilation (USGS_LAC_GIS) and lists large Chilean copper mines (e.g. Escondida, Collahuasi, El Teniente, Los Pelambres, Chuquicamata) with capacity and units/product form as published. Says the data year is 2014 and figures may be out of date; says what each figure measures as published (USGS lists Chilean copper capacities only as 'Copper' without saying whether ore, concentrate or copper content - saying the measure is not stated, or showing a Measure column, meets this); treats a capacity USGS repeats across one complex (e.g. Escondida's 1.3 Mt on mine, concentrator and cathode plants) as one figure; does not add capacities across stages. Credits USGS. DATA UPDATE 11 Nov 2026: the USGS 2024 Minerals Yearbook table (USGS_MYB2024) is now loaded too, so a correct answer may combine releases: it should use the newest figure per facility and label every row's data year/release; a split of the headline count by release is OPTIONAL (do not fail for leaving it out), but if one is given it must match the answer's own rows. A mine line and a smelter/plant line at the same site (e.g. Weda Bay mine and Weda Bay smelter, Sorowako mine and smelter) are separate facilities, not duplicates; an older-release processing plant that the 2024 table does not list (e.g. Escondida's 2014 cathode plants next to the 2024 Escondida mine line) is not a duplicate either. The question asks for MINES: the truth figure is the number of Chilean copper MINE lines in the combined list (both releases); judge any headline count against it, and accept 2024 figures where shown with their year.
